newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian King vows to stay politically neutral.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian King vows to stay politically neutral.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk returned to China for medical treatment on Sunday after pledging to remain politically neutral in the volatile world of Cambodian politics.
Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who maintain a fragile working relationship as co-premiers, were among the top leaders and diplomats at Pocheontong Airport to see the king off.
Sinhanouk, in a message dated Saturday and received on Sunday, said he would not enter politics, take part in elections or help any political party as long as he lives.
Analysts saw his words as intended to reassure Hun Sen of the formerly communist Cambodian People's Party (CPP), who earlier this year alluded to an alleged royalist plot against him and his party.
Ranariddh told reporters at the airport that Sihanouk's statement was intended "to calm somebody down, and you know who (that) is...he will be a real constitutional king."

The row between the CPP and Ranariddh's royalist FUNCIPEC party began in March when the prince demanded a greater share of power to reflect his party's narrow win in the U.N.-run national elections in 1993.
Ranariddh threatened to pull out of the government, prompting a warning from Hun Sen that he would use force to stop any effort to dismantle the coalition and parliament.
Tempers later calmed, but tensions have resurfaced over how to deal with defectors from the Khmer Rouge guerrilla movement.
Sihanouk, who turned 74 on October 31, was to receive medical treatment in China. His date of return was not known.
The king beat cancer earlier this year, but was then temporarily paralysed by a stroke that forced him to cut back his work schedule and improve his diet.
"Since this second stroke...I have become physically very weak, and long and tiring trips are forbidden to me by my doctors," he said in a statement last week.
